vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2374: feat(review): CodeRabbit integration — opportunistic ingestion of reviews, never gating

plan.title: feat(review): CodeRabbit integration — opportunistic ingestion of reviews, never gating
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: CodeRabbit (an AI code-review SaaS) can surface actionable findings cheaply and complement our review convoy, but it reviews PRs only SOMETIMES (quota). Three failure modes must be prevented: (1) gating on absence — any code path that reads CodeRabbit state and blocks on its absence creates intermittent failures; (2) drift into structural paths — once an ingestion helper exists, a future change could wire it into the merge gate (blockerReasons, readyForMerge, verification); (3) unanswered review threads left on the PR. CodeRabbit is NOT installed today (no .coderabbit.yaml, zero 'coderabbit' references in src/, no reviews on recent PRs).
narratives.Proposal: Adopt CodeRabbit OPPORTUNISTICALLY and structurally NON-GATING. (1) Add a repo-root .coderabbit.yaml tuned with path filters and request_changes_workflow:false so CodeRabbit never requests changes. (2) Add src/lib/cloister/coderabbit-ingestion.ts with fetchCodeRabbitFindings({workspace,branch}) that resolves the PR and reads coderabbitai[bot] review comments, returning [] on EVERY failure mode (absence indistinguishable from CodeRabbit-passed). (3) Wire findings into the EXISTING advisory-context seam buildReviewContextPromise (src/lib/cloister/review-context.ts) — mirroring stubUiFindings — so they surface to all four convoy reviewers and the synthesis agent via formatTier1Summary as ADVISORY context, never as a verdict. (4) Provide a minimal postCodeRabbitReply helper + canonical templates so cheap models reply to CodeRabbit threads consistently. (5) Lock the non-gating invariant structurally: a lint-guard + unit test asserting the full merge-advance surface never references 'coderabbit', PLUS an assertion that the ingestion module never touches setReviewStatus/blockerReasons/readyForMerge.
narratives.NonGoals:
- CodeRabbit must NEVER block merges or gate on absence — a missing review is treated identically to a passed review.
- CodeRabbit findings must NEVER become blockerReasons and must never set reviewStatus/testStatus/verificationStatus/uatStatus/readyForMerge.
- Do NOT extend webhook-handlers.ts (handlePullRequestReview) to treat coderabbitai reviews as changes_requested blockers.
- No structured severity/file/line parsing beyond the advisory summary block — follow-on hardening.
- No GitHub Marketplace app installation — that is an operator step outside these code changes.
- No integration with the pan inspect or pan review CLI commands.
- No automatic CodeRabbit review-thread resolution — the reply helper is best-effort text only.

autoDecisions.summary: Inject CodeRabbit findings via the existing review-context.ts advisory seam (buildReviewContextPromise + formatTier1Summary), mirroring stubUiFindings, instead of threading a coderabbitBlock through the convoy spawn as the PRD draft proposed.
autoDecisions.rationale: The stubUiFindings/policyNotes pattern already gathers advisory external context in buildReviewContextPromise's Promise.all with a .catch, persists it to the manifest, and surfaces it to ALL reviewers plus the synthesis agent. Reusing it is a smaller, lower-risk change than editing the convoy spawn, and the PRD's cited convoy anchor (buildReviewSubRolePrompt) does not even exist (real symbol: buildConvoyPromptPromise).

autoDecisions.summary: Expand the non-gating guard's gate-file list from the PRD's 3 files to 5: add src/lib/cloister/auto-merge-eligibility.ts and src/lib/flywheel-merge-order.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: Enumerating every merge-advance gate found isAutoMergeEligible (auto-merge-eligibility.ts) and reviewRecordEligibility/computeMergeQueue (flywheel-merge-order.ts) also decide 'ready to advance/merge'. Omitting them would leave real gates uncovered by the invariant test.

autoDecisions.summary: Add an anti-blocker structural assertion: the guard test also fails if src/lib/cloister/coderabbit-ingestion.ts references setReviewStatus, blockerReasons, or readyForMerge.
autoDecisions.rationale: The gate-file grep only catches 'coderabbit' inside gate files; it would miss a call FROM the ingestion module INTO setReviewStatusSync({blockerReasons}). Guarding the ingestion module's outbound surface closes the drift path from both directions.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the response flow (FR-3) minimal — helper + templates + tests + documented calling convention; no automatic thread resolution.
autoDecisions.rationale: Karpathy simplicity-first: deterministic reply text from cheap models is the goal; full thread-resolution automation is speculative and out of scope for the non-gating core.

items.title: Add repo-root .coderabbit.yaml (non-blocking profile, path filters, quota note)

expected_outputs: .coderabbit.yaml parses as valid YAML with exit code 0

narrative.Action: Create .coderabbit.yaml at the repo root. Set reviews.request_changes_workflow: false (CodeRabbit never requests changes / never blocks — the load-bearing non-gating key), reviews.profile: chill, and path_filters excluding generated/records paths: '!.pan/records/**', '!.beads/**', '!dist/**', '!*.map', '!.release/**', '!bun.lock', '!*.d.ts'. Add an inline comment documenting quota reality (CodeRabbit reviews only sometimes; absence must be indistinguishable from passed) and a comment linking https://docs.coderabbit.ai/getting-started/configuring-coderabbit for schema validation at install time. Independent of every other bead.

items.title: Given the repo root, a .coderabbit.yaml file exists there and parses as valid YAML (js-yaml load exits 0).
The reviews.path_filters list excludes .pan/records, .beads, dist, *.map, and .release paths.
reviews.request_changes_workflow defaults to false, and the file contains an inline comment documenting that CodeRabbit reviews only sometimes (quota) and that absence equals passed.
Add coderabbit-ingestion.ts: fetchCodeRabbitFindings (returns [] on every failure) + CodeRabbitFinding type

expected_outputs: coderabbit-ingestion.test.ts passes with the []-on-failure cases green

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/cloister/coderabbit-ingestion.ts (< 200 lines). Export an interface CodeRabbitFinding { path?: string; line?: number; body: string; url?: string } and export async function fetchCodeRabbitFindings(opts: { workspace: string; branch: string }): Promise<CodeRabbitFinding[]>. Implementation: resolve owner/repo in the workspace (e.g. `gh repo view --json owner,name` via execAsync, or existing repo-resolution), then lookupPullRequestNumberForBranch(owner, repo, branch) from src/lib/github-pr-lookup.ts; if null, return []. Then call `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/reviews?per_page=100` and `.../pulls/<n>/comments?per_page=100` via execAsync (promisified exec — NEVER execSync; mirror the pattern at src/lib/overdeck/discussions.ts:239 and :272), filter to user.login === 'coderabbitai[bot]' (and drop DISMISSED reviews), map to CodeRabbitFinding, and return the union. Wrap the ENTIRE body in try/catch: on ANY error log '[coderabbit-ingestion] fetch failed — skipping: <msg>' and return []. Never throw. Add a file-top comment stating the quota invariant: [] means 'no findings / quota miss / error / absent' and callers MUST treat all four identically. This bead requires inspection (fast) because it establishes the module boundary and the []-on-all-failures safety contract that cr-wire-context, cr-reply, and cr-guard all depend on.

items.title: Given gh api returns no coderabbitai[bot] entries, fetchCodeRabbitFindings returns an empty array.
When the underlying gh api call rejects (network/quota error) or the PR cannot be resolved, fetchCodeRabbitFindings returns an empty array and never throws.

Given at least one coderabbitai[bot] review or inline comment is present, fetchCodeRabbitFindings returns findings whose entries contain the comment body (and file path when the source is an inline comment).
A grep of coderabbit-ingestion.ts produces zero execSync matches, and the module exports a CodeRabbitFinding type that typecheck accepts.
Surface CodeRabbit findings in review context (manifest + formatTier1Summary, advisory-only)

expected_outputs: review-context test asserting empty-findings output is unchanged passes

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/review-context.ts, add a codeRabbitFindings: CodeRabbitFinding[] field to the ReviewContextManifest interface (next to stubUiFindings) and to the formatTier1Summary Pick type. In buildReviewContextPromise, add fetchCodeRabbitFindings({ workspace, branch: currentBranch }).catch(() => []) as a fourth entry in the Promise.all at review-context.ts:455 (mirroring the scanStubUi .catch), and include codeRabbitFindings in the manifest object at :476. In formatTier1Summary, after the stubUiFindings block (~:422), render a section ONLY when codeRabbitFindings.length > 0, headed 'CodeRabbit findings (ADVISORY — non-gating; context, not acceptance criteria):', listing up to 10 entries as '  - <path?:line?> <body first ~200 chars>' with a '... and N more' overflow line. Emit NOTHING when the array is empty so output is byte-identical to today. Do NOT touch review-agent.ts. Sequential: depends on cr-ingest-module.

items.title: buildReviewContextPromise persists a codeRabbitFindings field into the written context.json manifest.
buildReviewContextPromise gathers codeRabbitFindings inside its Promise.all with a .catch that returns [], so a fetch failure never rejects the manifest build.
Given a manifest with a non-empty codeRabbitFindings, formatTier1Summary renders a section labelled advisory/non-gating containing the finding bodies.
Given a manifest with an empty codeRabbitFindings, formatTier1Summary output is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-change output (asserted by a unit test).
Add postCodeRabbitReply helper + canonical templates (reuse exported postPrComment)

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/review-verdict-feedback.ts, add `export` to the existing postPrComment function (review-verdict-feedback.ts:76) — purely additive, its current caller is unaffected. In src/lib/cloister/coderabbit-ingestion.ts add two canonical template constants: CODERABBIT_REPLY_ADDRESSED(finding) => `Thanks for the finding — addressed: ${finding}` and CODERABBIT_REPLY_REJECTED(finding, rationale) => `Thanks for the finding — after review we're not applying this: ${finding}. Rationale: ${rationale}`. Add export async function postCodeRabbitReply(prUrl: string, disposition: 'addressed' | 'rejected', finding: string, rationale?: string): Promise<boolean> that builds the appropriate template body and calls postPrComment(prUrl, body); return its boolean result, and return false (never throw) on error. Add a doc-comment showing the calling convention so cheap-model work agents call it consistently. This is a best-effort reply path; it MUST NOT read or write review status. Depends on cr-ingest-module (same module file).

items.title: Given disposition 'addressed', postCodeRabbitReply calls postPrComment with the addressed-template text containing the finding.
Given disposition 'rejected' with a rationale, postCodeRabbitReply calls postPrComment with the rejected-template text including that rationale.
When postPrComment rejects, postCodeRabbitReply returns false without throwing.
postPrComment is exported from review-verdict-feedback.ts and imported by postCodeRabbitReply (typecheck passes with the import).
Structural non-gating invariant: lint guard + unit test across the full merge-advance surface

expected_outputs: lint script prints the pass line and exits 0 on the current tree

narrative.Action: Create scripts/lint-no-coderabbit-merge-gate.sh (set -euo pipefail): for each GATE_FILE — src/lib/review-status.ts, src/lib/cloister/verification-runner.ts, src/lib/cloister/deacon-merge.ts, src/lib/cloister/auto-merge-eligibility.ts, src/lib/flywheel-merge-order.ts — grep -qi 'coderabbit' and fail (exit 1) with a message if found. Add package.json script 'lint:no-coderabbit-merge-gate': 'bash scripts/lint-no-coderabbit-merge-gate.sh' and append ' && npm run lint:no-coderabbit-merge-gate' to the 'lint' script. Create tests/unit/lib/cloister/no-coderabbit-merge-gate.test.ts that (a) reads each of the five gate files and asserts its lowercased content does NOT contain 'coderabbit'; and (b) reads src/lib/cloister/coderabbit-ingestion.ts and asserts it does NOT contain 'setReviewStatus', 'blockerReasons', or 'readyForMerge' — proving findings cannot reach the merge gate from the ingestion side. Depends on cr-ingest-module (the ingestion file must exist for assertion (b)).

items.title: scripts/lint-no-coderabbit-merge-gate.sh exits non-zero when the string 'coderabbit' (case-insensitive) appears in any of the five gate files, and exits 0 on the current tree.
npm run lint:no-coderabbit-merge-gate is wired into the npm run lint chain and exits 0.
no-coderabbit-merge-gate.test.ts asserts none of the five gate files contain 'coderabbit' (case-insensitive) and passes.
The same test asserts src/lib/cloister/coderabbit-ingestion.ts never references setReviewStatus, blockerReasons, or readyForMerge, and passes.
